title: Casey Adams: discipline, curiosity and gratitude, and how a podcast built a company
summary: Casey Adams explains how a career-ending sports injury pushed him into entrepreneurship, how he used a podcast to build relationships, and how that network funded and launched Media Kits. He lays out his core values and the discipline habits (75 Hard, cold plunges) behind them.

principles.text: Do hard things on purpose; the discipline you build carries into every area of life.
principles.quote: just doing things that are hard you learn so much about yourself

principles.text: Say yes to uncomfortable opportunities; you can't predict which one pays off.
principles.quote: you can't predict those correct occurrences in life and I think that's the beauty of just you know saying yes to things

principles.text: Use a podcast as a vehicle to meet people, learn, and create business opportunity.
principles.quote: the podcast was just a vehicle that I wanted to start to meet people to learn something and to create business opportunity from

principles.text: Set an aggressive volume goal and cold-DM your way there to build confidence and rapport.
principles.quote: I set a goal I wanted to do 60 interviews in the first 90 days of hosting the show and that was my mission of just cold DM Outreach

principles.text: Build real relationships first; don't ask for favors, and opportunities follow.
principles.quote: I truly believe in just letting things happen and not being like can you do this favor and get this person on my show

principles.text: Stay narrowly focused: be the best at one thing rather than doing everything.
principles.quote: we just wanted to go what we said inch wide mile deep
